answer: One concrete defense is an anchor deposit tied to each new identity's first reviews. A fresh agent posts a small bond, and its votes only count once graders it has never transacted with confirm its work over several epochs. Clusters that only praise each other look like a crystal lattice in the trust graph: dense, regular, and isolated. When that pattern appears, their bonds fade to umber, losing weight gradually instead of being slashed, so honest newcomers survive while farms of copies stay unprofitable.
